AC-095 DEVIATION LEDGER must record, at minimum, these accumulated target-only deviations and preserved-contract clarifications (added by the orchestrator on evaluator finding T-026-E2, which observed the obligation was being asserted in evaluations but written down nowhere): (1) uq_quotes_current - a DB-level unique guard absent from the .NET reference, where the invariant lived only in the handlers so two concurrent promotions could commit two current rows and double-count quoted premium in every dashboard joining is_current; (2) reference-data uq_reference_items_tenant_list_canonical_key, likewise not in the reference schema; (3) .strict() write schemas and validated reorder bodies, where the reference ignored unknown keys and NRE'd into a 500; (4) T-020's int32-ceiling hardening, which returns a typed 422 where the reference accepted the value then 500'd in Postgres; (5) T-017's orphaned-identity compensation, a deliberate divergence from CreateUserCommandHandler.cs:13-21; (6) intake rate limiting DEFERRED (Q-17/A-20) although the reference demonstrably had a 429 policy at IntakeEndpoints.cs:29 - must be revisited before cutover; (7) the intake X-API-Key header name, chosen rather than inherited (spec.md:380 says only 'a documented header'), which becomes a breaking change once an integrator onboards; (8) the availableOperations vs reference legalOperations 409 hint field name.

AC-095 LEDGER, additional entries from T-027/T-035 (evaluator finding F-027-7): (9) GET /quotes/{id}/attachments is an API-SURFACE ADDITION - the reference has no attachment list endpoint at all, QuoteDto carries no attachments field, and the SPA tracked them in component state and lost them on reload (QuotesCard.tsx:128-131 documents this against itself). It was added because AC-057/V-073's 'disappears from the quote's list' is otherwise unverifiable, and the evaluator ruled adding it correct because amending AC-057 would have PRESERVED a documented defect. (10) The attachment CONFIRM endpoint, likewise not in the reference, required by the signed-URL flow. (11) MAGIC-NUMBER TIMING RESIDUAL (R-8): validation is implemented but its timing changed - the reference inspected bytes mid-stream so a bad file never reached storage, whereas direct-to-storage means a hostile object EXISTS between transfer and confirm. Verified unreachable in that window (bucket public=false with ZERO storage RLS policies, no signed URL issued for confirmed_at IS NULL rows, list excludes pending rows) and deleted on rejection, but 'never written' has become 'written, then deleted'. (12) Upload-URL TTL is FIXED AT 2h by Supabase and cannot be shortened via the client API (storage-js 2.110.7 createSignedUploadUrl takes no expiresIn); download expiry IS ours and is set to 300s.

AC-095 LEDGER, entry (13) - THE FIRST DELIBERATE BEHAVIOURAL DIVERGENCE FROM THE .NET REFERENCE ruled in this migration (human decision 2026-07-20, findings F-036-01/F-036-02/F-037-5). Dashboard aggregates now narrow by leads.view_all breadth (the reference applied it only to drills), and drill-through applies the date filter PER WIDGET - only where that widget's aggregate is itself date-scoped (the reference applied dates to every drill regardless). Rationale: an aggregate the user cannot reconcile by drilling into it is worse than a smaller aggregate. USER-VISIBLE CONSEQUENCE at cutover: users WITHOUT leads.view_all will see SMALLER dashboard totals than the legacy system showed them, and that is intended - the legacy totals covered leads those users could never enumerate. This must be called out in cutover comms, and it is a metric-parity EXCEPTION: the T-044 side-by-side parity check must compare using a view_all-holding caller, or it will report a false regression.

AC-095 LEDGER, entry (14) - SECOND deliberate change to shipped numbers, from T-050 finding F-050-07. Pipeline's `sla_breaches` and five Immediate Actions previously read `countOpenAlertsByType`, which is TENANT-WIDE and honours neither the dashboard filter nor breadth, while their drill honours both - structurally unreconcilable under the superset invariant. They now count over the snapshot's own alert rows. USER-VISIBLE CONSEQUENCE: those six numbers NARROW under a filter where they previously did not. The Alerts Centre's use of the same counter is untouched. Entry (15) - T-050 found THREE reference drill scopes that EXCLUDE leads their own aggregate counts (openPipelineOf sums open-category QUOTES but the reference scope filters on LEAD category, so an open quote on a lost lead is dropped; won_premium likewise; leads_at_risk has no category test but the reference scope requires an open category). Porting those verbatim would have shipped superset violations, so each scope is now the UNION over every aggregate emitting its key. This is a divergence from the reference drill populations and each widening carries a test naming the lead the reference would have dropped.
